final_recommendation: The room converged on a negotiated settlement framework: FINMA commits to publishing a 14-day memo with prospective non-viability triggers (LCR 80%, CET1 5.125%), 72-hour advance notice requirements, and a binding UBS contractual carve-out for AT1 recovery with quarterly certification. Discovery paused for 21 days; litigation resumes only if day-30 certification fails or UBS deviates >2% from published waterfall.
minority_objections: Bondholder counsel initially demanded full litigation across four jurisdictions with no pause, viewing settlement as legitimizing FINMA's hierarchy inversion
Insurance observer flagged that post-publication adviser E&O claims remain live and could generate a four-year reinsurance tail even if settlement closes
key_conflicts: Litigation vs. settlement timing: bondholder counsel wanted immediate multi-jurisdiction filing; FINMA and institutional investors pushed 21-day pause to negotiate recovery mechanism
Adviser liability carve-out: bondholder counsel insisted post-publication E&O claims stay live; FINMA wanted full settlement scope to avoid reinsurance cascade
Recovery mechanism enforceability: bondholder group demanded funded escrow or contractual UBS carve-out; FINMA initially offered only procedural memo without binding dollar commitment
Emergency carve-out scope: bondholder counsel resisted any discretionary bypass of 72-hour notice; FINMA needed flexibility for rapid deterioration scenarios
key_concessions: FINMA agreed to publish prospective non-viability triggers (LCR 80%, CET1 5.125%) with ECB/PRA alignment in day-14 memo
FINMA committed to 72-hour advance notice and bondholder input window before future write-downs, with published audit trail if emergency carve-out invoked
FINMA locked UBS contractual carve-out as regulatory sign-off condition, with quarterly certification and joint monitor
Bondholder group paused discovery for 21 days and accepted day-30 certification as litigation trigger instead of immediate filing
Bondholder counsel accepted that settlement scope covers only pre-publication AT1 claims, leaving post-publication adviser E&O exposure live
red_lines: Bondholder group: no settlement without binding UBS dollar commitment (escrow or contractual carve-out) and day-30 certification deadline
Institutional investor: will not hold $2.4B position past day 15 without ECB/PRA alignment on triggers and enforceable UBS waterfall
Bondholder counsel: emergency carve-out must require same-day publication of threshold breach; no discretionary bypass without audit trail
FINMA: will not reopen capital structure hierarchy or admit write-down was unlawful; settlement must preserve viability-event legal basis
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Systemic AT1 market repricing beyond Credit Suisse: room focused on CS-specific recovery but deferred broader market confidence to 'wait for Tier-1 issuer to print at sub-500bp'
Enforcement risk if UBS ignores carve-out post-close: quarterly monitor mitigates but does not eliminate risk that UBS drags certification or disputes waterfall calculation
Reinsurance accumulation across financial lines: insurance observer flagged E&O tail but room did not model cumulative exposure across D&O, E&O, and regulatory defense policies
Derivative shareholder suits piggy-backing bondholder discovery: mentioned in R1 but not developed as structured tail risk or settlement scope issue
downstream_risk_variables: Day-30 UBS certification outcome: if certification fails or deviates >2% from published waterfall, litigation resumes across three jurisdictions
Tier-1 issuer AT1 issuance pricing: market confidence hinges on whether Deutsche/BNP/HSBC can print at sub-500bp and hold for 30 days post-settlement
ECB/PRA enforcement of aligned triggers: if ECB or PRA deviate from LCR 80%/CET1 5.125% in future crises, Swiss-only precedent perception returns
Post-publication adviser E&O claims: if FINMA's advisers face negligence suits for non-enforcement of UBS carve-out, reinsurance tail runs four years minimum
Emergency carve-out invocation: if FINMA bypasses 72-hour notice in next crisis without publishing threshold breach same-day, procedural challenge resumes
uncertainty_notes: Settlement framework is contingent on three unresolved variables: (1) whether UBS honors day-30 certification and waterfall allocation within 2% tolerance, (2) whether a major Tier-1 issuer successfully prints AT1 at tighter spreads within 60 days to signal systemic confidence reset, and (3) whether post-publication adviser E&O claims materialize and trigger reinsurance denials, reopening discovery on FINMA's stress-testing and adviser selection. Room achieved procedural consensus but deferred enforcement and market-confidence risks to post-settlement monitoring.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was central in R1-R2 (bondholder counsel threatened immediate four-jurisdiction filing, discovery momentum peaked at 42), but room pivoted to 21-day pause and settlement framework by R3. Litigation became contingent trigger (day-30 certification failure) rather than dominant path.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: FINMA's legal basis (viability event, emergency ordinance) was contested in R1-R3 (bondholder counsel: 'FINMA changed the law in 72 hours'), but room accepted FINMA's contractual defense and shifted to procedural safeguards (advance notice, audit trail) rather than challenging write-down legality itself.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion (equity preserved, AT1 wiped) was the driving grievance throughout (R1: '150 years of capital hierarchy inverted'; R7: '$16B wiped while equity walked'). Room's entire settlement structure (UBS carve-out, waterfall quantification, quarterly certification) was designed to address this precedent damage.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing and frozen issuance was a central, recurring theme (R1-R8). Institutional investor's $2.4B hold decision, credit analyst's 'sub-500bp Tier-1 issuance' test, and ECB/PRA alignment requirement all structured around restoring market confidence. Marker peaked at 55 in R6.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year litigation tail was developed in R1 ('claims tail runs through 2030 minimum'), R3 (four-jurisdiction derivative suits), and R6-R8 (reinsurance layers, E&O coverage denials). Room structured settlement to contain tail (21-day pause, quarterly monitor) but left post-publication adviser claims live, acknowledging four-year exposure.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O exposure surfaced in R1 ('financial-lines litigation the moment insurers deny coverage') and was developed in R5-R8 (insurance observer repeatedly flagged reinsurance accumulation, E&O carrier denials, four-year tail). Room carved out post-publication adviser liability explicitly, acknowledging live E&O risk but not modeling cumulative financial-lines exposure.
